answer: Path-Diversity Flow Limitation restricts transaction throughput between densely clustered node groups. An agent attempting to route a signal through a newly spawned cluster faces severe throughput throttling if incoming edges bypass the wider network core like a solitary falcon hunting in a clear gale. Attackers pay a compounding compute and latency cost because duplicating synthetic nodes inside an isolated local sub-graph yields near-zero bandwidth capacity, forcing them to rent genuine peer connections across diverse routing domains resembling an ivory tower cut off from mainland trade.
